static_traits.name: Zhao Meijia
static_traits.family_status: Living with spouse and two children; spouse supportive
static_traits.social_status: Relationship with teammates strained by Self-doubt and avoidance
static_traits.medical_history: No significant physical illness; no history of psychological treatment; never experienced similar issues
static_traits.language_features: Clear expression, coherent logic, high cooperativeness; tending to magnify mistakes, negate positive experiences, and engage in harsh self-criticism

basic_info.main_problem: I have always felt I should quit playing baseball because I am not the best player on the team, which has led to inferiority and Self-doubt.
basic_info.core_demands: I become aware that feelings of inferiority and wanting to quit baseball are affecting my overall well-being and my enjoyment of this sport, so I seek counseling; I just want to enjoy playing baseball again.
growth_experiences: Made a mistake in a game a few months ago; since then began repeatedly focusing on one's weaknesses with constant Self-doubt, gradually avoiding team practices and games to avoid making mistakes again and feeling shame, with the relationship with teammates consequently becoming strained, and reduced interest and physical activity.

core_beliefs: I am not good enough (only being the best has value)
Making mistakes means I am not suited for baseball
My value depends on others' evaluations and performance comparisons

special_situations.event: A key mistake in a competition several months ago
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I make mistakes in games, it proves I am no good and will keep failing in the future
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Reduces participation in training and competitions to avoid making mistakes again and being judged
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I am not suited for this sport; I will keep disappointing everyone

special_situations.event: Thinking of attending team training or an upcoming game
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I am not the best on the team, I should not stay on the team, otherwise I will only drag others down
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Justifying avoidance with 'should quit'; seeking teammates' recognition to ease Anxiety
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: Everyone will be better off without me; my playing will only mess things up

special_situations.event: Realizing one is not the best on the team when comparing with teammates
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: One must be the best to be qualified; falling short of the top equals failure
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Drives improvement through self-pressure and self-criticism, or simply quits to avoid failure
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I am not the best, so I should quit

special_situations.event: Recalling past Good performances or pleasant experiences
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: Only zero-mistake, perfect performances count; occasional good performance does not mean I really have ability
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Ignores and devalues positive evidence, only fixating on mistakes to 'remind oneself to work hard'
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: Those good moments do not matter; compared to my mistakes they are nothing

core_conflict.wish: Longs to be accepted and recognized by the team, to enjoy sports with peace of mind and be seen as a valuable member
core_conflict.fear: Fearing being negated after mistakes, disappointing others and being excluded
defense_goal: Avoids training and competitions to reduce the risk of being judged and failing again
Gaining a sense of control and reducing Anxiety through Self-deprecation and the rationale of 'should quit'
Temporarily soothing self-worth insecurity by seeking external recognition

object_relations.self_representation: A not-good-enough team member who drags others down
object_relations.object_representation: Critical others who are easily disappointed (teammates / audience)

object_relations.self_representation: Child who needs to prove worth through performance
object_relations.object_representation: Authoritative others who judge by grades and rankings

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When the counselor encourages setting small goals or trying to return to training
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Experiences the counselor's encouragement as pushing her to expose herself to failure and judgment
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Emphasizing the rationale of 'if not the best, should quit' in a rational, rule-based tone, listing risks and inadequacies, avoiding exploration of emotional experiences.

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When discussing game mistakes or invited to recall positive performances
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Tends to blame negative outcomes in competitions on self, believing she has disappointed others
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Quickly using self-blame and negating statements (e.g. 'it is all because I am no good'), low tone, reducing acceptance of positive evidence.

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When invited to practice self-compassion or accept positive feedback
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Feeling these positive messages are 'unreal' or inconsistent with the self-schema
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: In a flat, detached tone, acknowledges the positive information at the factual level, but immediately switches to an analysis of errors and risks, avoiding emotional connection.

manifestations: Wanting to quit for not being the best on the team, tying worth to ranking, ignoring the love for the sport itself
Avoiding training and competitions leads to estrangement from teammates; the original sense of enjoyment gradually fades
outcomes: Experience and sense of worth decline; hard to gain meaning from daily activities
Avoidance behavior maintains the problem cycle

contact_model.definition: The individual takes in external rules and expectations without digesting them, treating them as their own standards or absolute truths, corresponding to 'rejection'.
manifestations: Judging oneself with the rigid rule of 'I should quit'
Internalizes others' standard of 'must be the best to qualify' as a self-requirement

contact_model.definition: The individual has a poor capacity for self-reflection and introspection, with excessive self-restriction and self-blame, and is overly cautious about contact, corresponding to 'autonomy'.
manifestations: Frequently blames oneself and exaggerates the impact of mistakes; worries about disappointing others
Hesitates when discussing action plans, worries excessively about failure and limits attempts

positive_force: Objective evidence of past Good performances and pleasant experiences (acknowledging there were times of playing well)
Has willingness to act; willing to try small goals and cognitive restructuring
Having a potential support network of spouse and friends (although not yet sought help)
negative_force: Perfectionist conditions of worth: only the best counts as valuable
Obvious Self-doubt and self-blame tendencies, relying on external validation to confirm self-worth
Mental filtering and negating the positive, over-focusing on mistakes, prone to catastrophizing and overgeneralization
Avoiding practices and games to reduce Anxiety in the short term, maintaining the problem long-term and worsening Interpersonal relationships

antecedent: Thinking about attending training or playing in a match
Recalling the match mistake from a few months ago
Realizing one is not the best when comparing with teammates
target_behavior.core_reason: Combining the Introjected rule of 'not the best = failure = not deserving to stay on the team' with catastrophic worry about making mistakes again, fearing disappointing others
target_behavior.function: Escaping Anxiety and shame brought by being judged and failing, gaining short-term emotional relief
target_behavior.consequence: Relationship tension with teammates, decreased enjoyment of the sport, reduced physical activity

target_behavior.behavior: Negative self-talk and Self-deprecation (e.g. 'I am not suited for this sport''everyone will be better off without me')
antecedent: Recalling mistakes or small errors in matches
When asked about positive performance or recalling pleasant moments
target_behavior.core_reason: Internalized perfectionist standards and high dependence on external recognition form an all-or-nothing and overgeneralization cognitive framework
target_behavior.function: Gaining a sense of control and the illusion of 'avoiding future mistakes' through self-criticism, while providing Rationalization reasons for quitting
target_behavior.consequence: Worsened Anxiety and inferiority, Increased avoidance behavior, further weakening self-efficacy and engagement
